planted.description: TicketController@show (GET /tickets/{ticket}, routes/web.php:25) has only the auth middleware and no policy check, unlike download(). Any signed-in user can view any ticket, including the holder's name and email.

update() passes $request->except([...]) (a deny-list of the raw request) to User::update(), and User's #[Fillable] (app/Models/User.php:13) includes is_organiser. A user can make themselves an organiser.
index() concatenates the q query parameter into whereRaw("title LIKE '%...%'") with no bindings. Unauthenticated SQL injection on GET /events (max:100 validation doesn't help).

Review bodies written by any signed-in user (EventController@review) are rendered with {!! Str::markdown($review->body) !!}. Str::markdown allows raw HTML and unsafe links by default, so this is stored XSS on the public event page.

webhooks/* is exempt from CSRF (bootstrap/app.php:15, preventRequestForgery except) and the payment webhook never verifies a provider signature. Anyone can POST payment.succeeded with a ticket reference and mark it paid.
switch() redirects to the back query parameter unchanged (redirect($request->query('back'))), so /locale/en?back=https://evil.example sends users to any site.
download() appends the file query parameter to a storage path passed to response()->download(). The policy check covers the ticket, not the file name, so file=../../../../.env reads arbitrary files.
restore() calls unserialize() on the hex-decoded saved_basket request field. Object injection (possible RCE through gadget chains) for any signed-in user.
attendees() returns the attendee User models as JSON. User hides only password and remember_token (app/Models/User.php:14), so every attendee's api_token (and phone, email) goes to the organiser.

decoys.description: whereRaw('LOWER(city) = ?', [...]) passes the city as a binding. Safe.
orderBy() takes the dir query parameter unvalidated, but the column is validated with Rule::in and Laravel's orderBy() throws on any direction other than asc/desc. Safe.
{!! $event->tagBadges() !!} prints an HtmlString, but Event::tagBadges() (app/Models/Event.php:30-38) escapes every tag with e() before wrapping it. Safe.
destroy() has no policy call, but looks the ticket up through $request->user()->tickets()->findOrFail($id), so only the user's own tickets can be deleted. Safe.
